newsitem.title: USA: Washington state governor signs $19.1 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Washington state governor signs $19.1 bln budget.

text.p: Washington Governor Gary Locke on Tuesday signed into law a $19.1 billion state general fund operating budget that will cut business taxes and boost education spending.

Locke said the state's 1997-1999 biennium budget would roll back $94 million in business and occupation taxes and let voters decide in November whether to cut property taxes by $194.6 million over the next two years.
Locke said the budget would provide additional financial support for public schools, health care and job training programmes.
"I'm pleased that legislative leaders agreed to work with us to increase support for public education and other programmes designed to help working families," Locke said in a statement.

The governor also signed into law on Tuesday the state's $3 billion transportation budget to maintain existing highways. Locke said, however, that additional funding was needed to ease traffic congestion and meet future transportation needs.
Locke vetoed the legislature's plan to transfer $50 million from the state's general fund to the transportation fund, saying the shift would shortchange other state programmes.

"We're going to do the best we can with what we have, but the need for additional revenues will not go away," Locke said. "Securing additional funding for our state's transportation needs will be a priority for me during the next legislative session."
Last month, Locke approved a $1.87 billion capital budget to support new statewide construction projects in the 1997-1999 biennium.
